setting: A self-replicating extinction-vector tore through an alien civilization, but its makers are not dead — they are SEALED. They went into quarantine-sleep behind their own unfinished containment, dormant in vaults alongside the dormant carriers of the thing that hunted them; waking either is the threat. The story is PRESENT TENSE: the vector still sleeps in sealed worlds and stirs in drifting carriers, and a human colony has just arrived inside its range. The engine is CONTAINMENT, not extraction — hunting quarantine-relics and the scattered fragments of a forward-facing containment recipe (identify the vector -> find its dormancy trigger -> locate the keystone relic -> assemble the seal) is a race to finish the seal the makers never completed, where every relic cracked might reseed the plague here, now.

civs.name: the-cradlekeepers
civs.trait: the makers themselves, sealed in quarantine-sleep behind their own unfinished containment; wakeable as allies — or already carriers, no one knows which vault holds which

civs.name: the-stillborn-host
civs.trait: sleepers the vector reached first; dormant carriers whose waking is itself the outbreak, sealed beside the makers they can no longer be told apart from

civs.name: the-vector
civs.trait: the extinction-agent itself — nanite swarm, mind-virus, or engineered pathogen depending on the world — sleeping in the relics' lore and the carriers' marrow, stirring whenever a seal is broken

climax_label: the seal that was never finished
